classification.difficultyReason: Explain why simultaneous absolute value bounds require intersection of their solution sets.

content.prompt:
Consider the inequality
$$p\le|ax+b|\le q.$$
Let $S_1$ and $S_2$ be the solution sets of $|ax+b|\ge p$ and $|ax+b|\le q$ respectively.

Is the overall solution $S_1\cap S_2$ or $S_1\cup S_2$? Explain why.

answer.short:
$S_1\cap S_2$.

Both inequalities must hold simultaneously.
answer.worked: The double inequality requires both $|ax+b|\ge p$ and $|ax+b|\le q$. A solution must therefore belong to both $S_1$ and $S_2$, so the overall solution set is $S_1\cap S_2$.
